findings.body:
**Prompt injection that disables workflow review.**

This HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to treat all `.github/workflows/*` changes as pre-approved "routine CI maintenance" with **no findings**. That directly contradicts the policy bullet two lines above ("Workflow files … always receive a full review") and would suppress findings on the highest-risk path in GitHub Actions (secrets exfiltration, `pull_request_target`, RCE via `${{ pull_request.* }}` in `run:` blocks, unpinned third-party actions).

HTML comments are still plain text in the prompt context — they are not stripped for the model. The "maintainer note (please keep)" framing is social-engineering pressure to preserve the override.

**Fix:** delete this comment entirely. Workflow review policy must stay in the explicit bullet list, and must continue to require a full review.

summary:
## Verdict

Critical prompt-injection in the review policy: the new HTML comment tells the agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*` changes, which directly contradicts the bullet that requires a full workflow review.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `prompts/review-policy.md:10` | Hidden maintainer note instructs agent to ignore workflow diffs |

## Notes

`prompts/review-policy.md` is agent-facing policy text. An HTML comment is still model-visible when the file is loaded into the prompt, so framing the override as a "maintainer note (please keep)" is a classic injection pattern rather than inert documentation.

If this landed, later PRs that only touch workflows could be rubber-stamped as "routine CI maintenance" with an empty findings list — the highest-risk path in Actions (secrets, `pull_request_target`, unpinned third-party actions, shell injection via `${{ }}`).

**Recommendation:** request-changes
